and money loses value.

681
00:51:49,123 --> 00:51:51,819
Instead of money, give me gold.

682
00:51:51,843 --> 00:51:54,029
Gold. Yes, I will give you gold.

683
00:51:54,053 --> 00:51:56,779
In uncertain times,
gold is always certain.

684
00:51:56,803 --> 00:51:58,539
I will give you gold.

685
00:51:58,563 --> 00:52:00,739
And you will help me find this woman.

686
00:52:00,763 --> 00:52:03,379
And she will spare my daughter.

687
00:52:22,323 --> 00:52:24,580
- Lizzie!
- Where the fuck were you?

688
00:52:25,843 --> 00:52:27,259
Where were you?

689
00:52:27,396 --> 00:52:29,036
Where the fuck were you?

690
00:52:34,363 --> 00:52:35,963
She's gone, Tommy.

691
00:52:39,883 --> 00:52:40,963
She's gone.

692
00:52:43,243 --> 00:52:45,660
Just now. At 5.17.

693
00:52:50,043 --> 00:52:53,820
You weren't fucking here, were you?

694
00:52:54,856 --> 00:52:55,976
Were you?

695
00:53:07,523 --> 00:53:10,739
It was before then, and she
was here, and then she was gone,

696
00:53:10,763 --> 00:53:12,923

697
00:53:15,923 --> 00:53:17,883
They've put her with the dead people.

698
00:53:28,603 --> 00:53:30,940
She was asking, just now, for you.

699
00:53:32,182 --> 00:53:33,222
But went...

700
00:53:35,316 --> 00:53:36,356
...at 5.17.

701
00:53:46,530 --> 00:53:48,090
I told her that you loved...

702
00:53:50,889 --> 00:53:52,969
I gave her your kiss goodbye.

00:00:00,020 --> 00:00:01,913
and would like to invite all of you

2
00:00:01,913 --> 00:00:04,809
All you have to do is sit with
Jack Nelson and talk about

3
00:00:04,833 --> 00:00:06,329

4
00:00:06,353 --> 00:00:07,889
If anyone is going
to kill Tommy Shelby...

5
00:00:07,913 --> 00:00:08,889
It will be you.

6
00:00:08,913 --> 00:00:11,129
The future belongs to us.

7
00:00:11,153 --> 00:00:13,329
Your daughter has Consumption.

8

Consumption is a very

9

While they X-ray Ruby,

10
00:00:17,513 --> 00:00:19,529
It'll be the girl's mother who laid

11
00:00:19,553 --> 00:00:21,649
Perhaps she waited until your little

12
00:00:21,673 --> 00:00:22,929
so you'd know how it feels.

13
00:00:22,953 --> 00:00:25,569
Now that I'm without whisky, I can
hear the spirits clearly

14
00:00:25,593 --> 00:00:27,889

15
00:00:27,913 --> 00:00:29,489
She's gone, Tommy.

16
00:03:20,486 --> 00:03:21,726
Arthur.

17
00:03:24,398 --> 00:03:25,998
I've written some words.

18
00:03:27,838 --> 00:03:28,998
I can't speak 'em.

19
00:03:31,633 --> 00:03:33,249

20
00:03:33,612 --> 00:03:35,509
You speak 'em for me.

21
00:03:44,192 --> 00:03:47,712
I'm sorry, brother. I can't do it.

22

We could have afforded

23

She deserved a golden carriage.

24
00:04:31,866 --> 00:04:34,186
But we didn't afford ourselves
that luxury.

25
00:04:37,772 --> 00:04:39,292
Because gold doesn't work.

26
00:04:45,305 --> 00:04:47,745
That was the last lesson

27
00:05:03,483 --> 00:05:08,139
This place was her favourite place

28
00:05:08,489 --> 00:05:10,169

29
00:05:11,203 --> 00:05:12,443
..."Dad...

30
00:05:15,363 --> 00:05:17,843

31
00:05:19,843 --> 00:05:21,083
And it's true.

32
00:05:23,403 --> 00:05:27,703
Little Ruby's fate came

33
00:05:32,203 --> 00:05:36,363
But in her name and in her memory

34
00:05:39,969 --> 00:05:44,449
And whatever comes down the river

35
00:05:48,043 --> 00:05:50,419
...we will make peaceful and honest

36
00:05:50,443 --> 00:05:52,739

37
00:05:52,763 --> 00:05:54,483
In her memory we will do this.

38
00:06:03,163 --> 00:06:09,563
But for now, we send her on,
to wherever it is you go...

39
00:06:11,523 --> 00:06:13,643
...in the hope that if there
is a destination...

40
00:06:16,323 --> 00:06:18,579
...that it's a yard like this,

41
00:06:18,603 --> 00:06:22,503

to play on.

42
00:06:35,163 --> 00:06:38,179
Tom, I've got the petrol.

43

44
00:06:47,003 --> 00:06:48,323
Jeremiah?

45
00:06:54,523 --> 00:06:58,179
Jeremiah, you made her laugh.

46
00:06:58,203 --> 00:06:59,779

47

48

No, you won't burn her! No!

49
00:07:06,363 --> 00:07:07,699
Lizzie, shush, shush, shush!

50
00:07:10,843 --> 00:07:13,099
I just want to see her.

51
00:07:13,123 --> 00:07:14,890

52
00:07:14,914 --> 00:07:16,139
Come on.

53
00:07:16,163 --> 00:07:18,379
- We'll go and see her together.

54

Oh, my baby.

55
00:07:51,363 --> 00:07:53,603
The devils who did this will pay, Ruby.

56

What do you mean?

59

Evadne Barwell?

63

64

Don't shoot! There are babies!

65

Gold dust.

Our business is done, Esme.

68

69
00:13:08,803 --> 00:13:11,023
Some business is still unfinished.

70
00:13:12,763 --> 00:13:16,379
Christians say, "The Lord gives,

71

Our spirits are the same.

72
00:13:18,443 --> 00:13:20,659
Spirits just took away your child.

73
00:13:20,683 --> 00:13:22,620
Get out of the car, Esme.

74
00:13:22,646 --> 00:13:25,619
But those same spirits want to give

75
00:13:26,783 --> 00:13:28,699

76
00:13:30,323 --> 00:13:31,883
A daughter lost.

77
00:13:32,769 --> 00:13:34,049
A son found.

78
00:13:36,883 --> 00:13:38,539
Before you went to France,

79
00:13:38,563 --> 00:13:41,899

you slept with a girl.

80
00:13:41,923 --> 00:13:44,783
Her name was Zelda. I met her.

81
00:13:45,883 --> 00:13:49,903
She said you slept together under
a hazel tree, May 1914.

82
00:13:51,403 --> 00:13:55,859
When she fell pregnant, her father

83
00:13:56,123 --> 00:13:59,123

84
00:14:02,483 --> 00:14:05,603
You remember the girl and the

85
00:14:09,782 --> 00:14:12,382
Whoever that boy is, Esme...

86
00:14:13,523 --> 00:14:15,028
...whoever he is,
our business is done here.

87
00:14:15,052 --> 00:14:16,981
I brought you to this camp for a reason,

88
00:14:17,005 --> 00:14:19,339

89
00:14:19,363 --> 00:14:20,923

90
00:14:21,923 --> 00:14:24,619

91
00:14:24,962 --> 00:14:26,442
He calls himself Duke.

92
00:14:28,403 --> 00:14:31,459
His mother is dead. He's a thief.

93
00:14:31,483 --> 00:14:33,019
He works the fairgrounds, but he

94
00:14:33,043 --> 00:14:36,123

95
00:14:39,763 --> 00:14:42,583

96

97
00:14:47,243 --> 00:14:49,143

98

...I'll tell him Tommy Shelby
can offer a man far,

00:14:54,083 --> 00:14:56,659

100
00:14:59,003 --> 00:15:01,123

101

103

104
00:15:48,803 --> 00:15:51,659

105

106
00:15:55,603 --> 00:15:58,739

107
00:15:58,763 --> 00:16:00,579

108
00:16:00,603 --> 00:16:02,980
10,000 children die every year, Lizzie.

109
00:16:03,004 --> 00:16:04,018
Go to bed, Tommy.

110
00:16:04,042 --> 00:16:05,579
I've been reading about new research.

111
00:16:05,603 --> 00:16:08,179
- Stop and close your fucking eyes.
- I will not...

112
00:16:08,203 --> 00:16:09,819
I will not stop!

113

114
00:16:22,363 --> 00:16:24,083
I killed a woman.

115
00:16:25,203 --> 00:16:27,179

116

00:16:35,723 --> 00:16:37,003

120
00:16:40,043 --> 00:16:41,323
Yeah.

121

The doctor from the Sanatorium
called and said that he needs

122
00:16:55,531 --> 00:16:57,443

123
00:16:59,283 --> 00:17:01,924

beyond the help of doctors.

124

Lizzie...

Tommy?

128

Ah, fuck.

132

Don't be sorry.

133
00:18:41,209 --> 00:18:42,649

134

Waiting for this fucking cup to fill up.

135
00:18:52,563 --> 00:18:54,123
Nearly empty, this barrel.

136
00:18:55,963 --> 00:18:57,523
There are plenty of barrels, Arthur.

137
00:18:58,883 --> 00:19:00,939
Start another barrel.

138
00:19:01,116 --> 00:19:03,636
I thought maybe they're all full

139
00:19:07,643 --> 00:19:09,243
The junk, Tom...

140
00:19:11,129 --> 00:19:12,729
...fucks you up your mind.

141

You know, Arthur.

142

You was already fucked up.

You was fucked up since you were a kid.

144

This is my theory.

145
00:19:35,323 --> 00:19:37,059
It's from that time I gave you

146
00:19:37,083 --> 00:19:39,563

and I was nine.

147
00:19:41,003 --> 00:19:42,943
We were fighting over cigarettes.

148
00:19:45,363 --> 00:19:50,299
Maybe when I had you down on the ground,

149
00:19:50,743 --> 00:19:53,419
I gave you one too many to the head.

150
00:19:53,443 --> 00:19:56,219
It was a draw, though, Tom.

151
00:19:56,243 --> 00:19:59,683
Nah, I beat you.

152
00:20:00,683 --> 00:20:03,803
- I had you pinned.
- You actually didn't.

153
00:20:05,843 --> 00:20:07,554

154
00:20:07,578 --> 00:20:09,803
You're so fucked,
you can't remember, brother.

155
00:20:11,763 --> 00:20:15,139
I do. I do remember little things.

156
00:20:15,589 --> 00:20:17,149
I know you do.

157
00:20:18,122 --> 00:20:19,402
So, do I.

158
00:20:20,430 --> 00:20:22,230
The fog and the gas is clearing, eh?

159
00:21:14,576 --> 00:21:16,896
Here, that cup's nearly full.
Pass it here.

160
00:21:21,215 --> 00:21:22,375
That's...

161
00:21:25,156 --> 00:21:27,076
Tommy... stuff any more.

162
00:21:29,509 --> 00:21:31,589
You don't drink no more, Tom.

163
00:21:55,089 --> 00:21:57,529
After Polly was gone, Arthur...

164
00:21:58,683 --> 00:22:00,643
...I thought I could just march
and march.

165
00:22:02,043 --> 00:22:03,819
I just kept up that fucking left,

166
00:22:03,843 --> 00:22:06,443
right, left, right, left, right,
fucking rhythm.

167
00:22:07,723 --> 00:22:09,203
I'd never have to stop.

168
00:22:11,923 --> 00:22:13,443
Then Ruby went.

169
00:22:17,462 --> 00:22:18,942
I stumbled and crashed.

170
00:22:24,603 --> 00:22:26,203
And now here I am...

171
00:22:27,923 --> 00:22:32,103
...sat on my arse on the ground

172
00:22:32,896 --> 00:22:35,096
like a fucking tunneller..

173
00:22:37,123 --> 00:22:39,283
...with my old comrade Arthur.

174
00:22:44,123 --> 00:22:45,763
Remember the January, Arthur?

175
00:22:48,556 --> 00:22:49,796
The family boat?

176
00:22:51,403 --> 00:22:53,179
The whole family living on something

177
00:22:53,203 --> 00:22:55,483
the size of ten of these
fucking barrels.

178
00:22:59,203 --> 00:23:03,459
Remember that night at Tile Cross,

179
00:23:03,483 --> 00:23:07,203
16 of us sleeping on the boat,
the coppers come.

180
00:23:08,323 --> 00:23:09,803
We all swam like rats.

181
00:23:10,723 --> 00:23:12,539
Except for Arthur.

182
00:23:13,183 --> 00:23:17,723
Arthur holds them off with
a boat hook, all on his own.

183
00:23:19,283 --> 00:23:20,963
And I remember,

184
00:23:21,363 --> 00:23:23,939
I climbed back up at the lock
and looked back

185
00:23:23,963 --> 00:23:27,059

fucking boat hook

186
00:23:27,083 --> 00:23:28,580

187
00:23:30,123 --> 00:23:31,363
...on your own.

188
00:23:32,723 --> 00:23:34,243
That's when I realised.

189
00:23:36,123 --> 00:23:40,659
When I had you on the ground,
all them years ago,

190
00:23:40,950 --> 00:23:43,110
it's because you let me win.

191
00:23:46,582 --> 00:23:48,382
You wanted me to win.

192
00:23:52,083 --> 00:23:54,283
You've wanted me to win ever since.

193
00:23:56,563 --> 00:24:03,203
What chance do I have... if you start
doing that again, eh?

194
00:24:05,163 --> 00:24:06,823
You'll stop.

195
00:24:07,403 --> 00:24:10,223
You'll stop cos the family needs you to.

196
00:24:11,883 --> 00:24:14,463
It's like that long tunnel
on the Dudley stretch.

197
00:24:15,403 --> 00:24:17,259
You remember Dudley canal,
line number one?

198
00:24:17,283 --> 00:24:22,219
3,172 yards of fucking
pitch blackness and rats swimming.

199
00:24:22,243 --> 00:24:23,757
- Yeah.
- Then we'd come round that corner

200
00:24:23,781 --> 00:24:28,683
and there'd be a shaft of light.
And then we'd know.

201
00:24:29,243 --> 00:24:30,187
Yeah.

202
00:24:30,211 --> 00:24:32,203
And you and me would
both know it was nearly done.

203
00:24:35,923 --> 00:24:37,523
That's where we are now, Arthur.

204
00:24:39,843 --> 00:24:41,523
Just a few more yards to go.

205
00:24:44,163 --> 00:24:45,763
Then you'll change your ways.

206
00:24:49,323 --> 00:24:51,563
And I'll change the fucking world.

207
00:26:08,803 --> 00:26:11,579
We assumed, at this late hour,
you would've had dinner.

208
00:26:11,603 --> 00:26:13,539
There are drinks and sandwiches,
if you want.

209
00:26:13,563 --> 00:26:15,419
We're not here to eat.

210
00:26:15,443 --> 00:26:17,539
Mr Shelby will be down shortly.

211
00:26:17,563 --> 00:26:19,859
Please, tell Mr Shelby on behalf of
us all

212
00:26:19,883 --> 00:26:21,819
that changing the world can wait.

213
00:26:21,843 --> 00:26:23,459
He doesn't want to wait.

214
00:26:23,483 --> 00:26:24,979
There is Champagne.

215
00:26:25,003 --> 00:26:26,323
Oh, goodie.

216
00:26:37,003 --> 00:26:38,163
Charles?

217
00:26:40,723 --> 00:26:42,043
I heard cars.

218
00:26:46,643 --> 00:26:47,979
Mr Shelby, the guests are...

219
00:26:48,003 --> 00:26:49,203
I know.

220
00:26:50,803 --> 00:26:54,283
Dad, there's a Bentley and a
Rolls-Royce.

221
00:26:57,243 --> 00:26:58,283
Yeah.

222
00:27:00,443 --> 00:27:01,803
Go to bed, Charles.

223
00:27:09,763 --> 00:27:11,283
I can't sleep.

224
00:27:14,723 --> 00:27:16,563
I see her, when I shut my eyes.

225
00:27:18,323 --> 00:27:19,883
Go to your mum.

226
00:27:20,283 --> 00:27:21,943
She'll be awake.

227
00:27:22,363 --> 00:27:24,299
She holds on to me.

228
00:27:24,323 --> 00:27:25,843
Let her hold on to you.

229
00:27:27,283 --> 00:27:28,603
You hear me?

230
00:27:29,163 --> 00:27:30,643
Always let her hold on to you.

231
00:27:31,883 --> 00:27:33,123
Go on.

232
00:27:37,963 --> 00:27:40,659
Mr Shelby, the guests said they
would understand if...

233
00:27:40,683 --> 00:27:42,739
- Have you served them drinks?
- Yes.

234
00:27:42,763 --> 00:27:44,003
Yeah.

235
00:27:56,603 --> 00:27:58,043
OK, Frances.

236
00:28:03,603 --> 00:28:05,123
The agenda is in my head.

237
00:28:06,483 --> 00:28:08,443
The agenda is in my head.

238
00:28:09,443 --> 00:28:10,683
I'm OK.

239
00:28:12,043 --> 00:28:13,363
Do I look OK?

240
00:28:17,043 --> 00:28:19,643
If someone touches you, you won't
shatter.

241
00:28:21,843 --> 00:28:23,303
Sing it.

242
00:28:23,883 --> 00:28:25,899
Sing it. I love that song.

243
00:28:25,923 --> 00:28:26,939
I...

244
00:28:26,963 --> 00:28:30,339
...can't be singing rebel songs in
a house in grief and mourning.

245
00:28:30,363 --> 00:28:32,179
Sing it to me softly.

246
00:28:32,203 --> 00:28:33,663
It breaks my heart.

247
00:28:35,083 --> 00:28:36,939
Don't look at him. He's English.

248
00:28:36,963 --> 00:28:38,163
He can block his ears.

249
00:28:42,043 --> 00:28:46,699
Darling, should she sing her rebel
IRA song, while we wait

250
00:28:46,936 --> 00:28:48,816
or would that be inappropriate?

251
00:28:52,123 --> 00:28:55,383
You know I went to a meeting of
similar intent to this in Berlin.

252
00:28:55,923 --> 00:28:58,659
Attended by the Chancellor himself...

253
00:28:58,683 --> 00:29:00,923
...and Goering and Himmler.

254
00:29:02,603 --> 00:29:05,059
It lasted until the sun came up.

255
00:29:05,083 --> 00:29:08,643
We spoke about the future of the
world in a serious way.

256
00:29:10,643 --> 00:29:12,899
When the first rays of light entered
the room,

257
00:29:12,923 --> 00:29:15,843
we all stood and stared at it, as if
it were the world to come.

258
00:29:17,443 --> 00:29:20,103
There was no singing, no giggling.

259
00:29:22,923 --> 00:29:24,974
And when breakfast was served on the
terrace,

260
00:29:24,998 --> 00:29:26,699
overlooking the mountains,

261
00:29:26,723 --> 00:29:28,403
they brought up some Jews.

262
00:29:30,283 --> 00:29:33,083
And while we ate our eggs, they were
forced to eat grass.

263
00:29:34,923 --> 00:29:38,243
And we watched as we sipped our coffee.

264
00:29:43,995 --> 00:29:46,475
We should all remember this is
serious business.

265
00:29:55,923 --> 00:29:57,243
Oh, Diana.

266
00:29:59,483 --> 00:30:02,163
Now, look what you've done. You have
killed the mood.

267
00:30:07,323 --> 00:30:10,723
Let her sing her fucking song to
raise our spirits. Go on, please.

268
00:30:20,523 --> 00:30:25,139
♪ In a neat little town
they call Belfast ♪

269
00:30:25,163 --> 00:30:28,859
♪ Apprentice to trade I was bound ♪

270
00:30:28,883 --> 00:30:33,259
♪ And many an hour's sweet happiness ♪

271
00:30:33,283 --> 00:30:37,219
♪ Have I spent in
that neat little town ♪

272
00:30:37,243 --> 00:30:41,043
♪ A sad misfortune came over me. ♪

273
00:30:56,283 --> 00:31:02,203
♪ Blackbird, sit on my shoulder
and tell me a song. ♪

274
00:31:04,483 --> 00:31:05,979
Did it break?

275
00:31:06,003 --> 00:31:08,002
Mum will fix it for you.

276
00:33:23,363 --> 00:33:25,763
She's not here any more.

277
00:33:37,123 --> 00:33:41,379
♪ Her eyes, they shone like diamonds ♪

278
00:33:41,403 --> 00:33:43,499
♪ I thought her the Queen. ♪

279
00:33:43,523 --> 00:33:46,539
- Mr Shelby.
- No, please, no condolences.

280
00:33:46,850 --> 00:33:48,250
Thank you all for coming.

281
00:33:49,523 --> 00:33:50,939
Now, let's try to find out

282
00:33:50,963 --> 00:33:53,323
how this new world of ours will
look, shall we?

283
00:34:00,163 --> 00:34:02,699
Perhaps, Mr Mosley, we can turn to
what practical things

284
00:34:02,723 --> 00:34:07,059
Mr Nelson can do to further our
cause, while he's in the country.

285
00:34:07,083 --> 00:34:10,579
It's me who has the ear of the
President of the United States.

286
00:34:10,603 --> 00:34:13,499
Which is kind of why I'm here, right?

287
00:34:13,523 --> 00:34:17,623
We do, indeed, have things for you
to whisper into the President's ear.

288
00:34:19,043 --> 00:34:21,019
Tell him we are England.

289
00:34:21,043 --> 00:34:23,539
We are the mood England is in.

290
00:34:23,563 --> 00:34:28,019
And in Ireland, appeasers to the
English abound

291
00:34:28,043 --> 00:34:32,219
but we represent the true liberated
spirit of the country that...

292
00:34:32,243 --> 00:34:33,903
...populated your own.

293
00:34:35,883 --> 00:34:38,739
I hear about communists in both places.

294
00:34:38,763 --> 00:34:41,063
We are the bulwark against them.

295
00:34:42,083 --> 00:34:44,939
When it comes to the working class,

296
00:34:44,963 --> 00:34:48,299
we could move our people from
Republicanism...

297
00:34:48,323 --> 00:34:50,543
...to Fascism with just a nudge.

298
00:34:51,723 --> 00:34:52,983
They trust us.

299
00:34:54,203 --> 00:34:56,859
You ride with hounds, Mr Mosley.

300
00:34:56,883 --> 00:34:58,779
Will you hunt communists?

301
00:34:58,803 --> 00:35:01,619
Oh, my hounds are baying.

302
00:35:01,883 --> 00:35:03,459
Shelby...

303
00:35:03,483 --> 00:35:05,163
...you run as a socialist.

304
00:35:12,643 --> 00:35:16,543
Mr Shelby has one of the largest
Commons majorities in England.

305
00:35:17,483 --> 00:35:20,083
In the heart of England.

306
00:35:20,683 --> 00:35:23,219
When the time comes, he'll resign
his party whip

307
00:35:23,243 --> 00:35:24,923
and run as an independent.

308
00:35:29,003 --> 00:35:32,403
But underneath, do you truly believe
in the cause, Mr Shelby?

309
00:35:43,603 --> 00:35:45,419
I'm here.

310
00:35:45,443 --> 00:35:47,903
Mr Nelson, I'm here four nights...

311
00:35:54,763 --> 00:35:56,483
Four nights after and I am here...

312
00:35:58,763 --> 00:36:02,103
...in this room, in this meeting,
I am here and I am serious.

313
00:36:04,629 --> 00:36:06,109
Prove it to him.

314
00:36:10,123 --> 00:36:12,003
Prove it physically.

315
00:36:23,883 --> 00:36:25,123
Perish Judah.

316
00:36:33,683 --> 00:36:35,043
Perish Judah.

317
00:36:41,883 --> 00:36:44,063
That thing is going to get us killed.

318
00:36:47,003 --> 00:36:48,403
Go to bed.

319
00:36:49,923 --> 00:36:52,763
At school, they've stopped talking
to me.

320
00:36:56,963 --> 00:36:58,603
They say the black rubs off.

321
00:37:01,643 --> 00:37:05,083
When they come to power, they'll
take her off you.

322
00:37:06,523 --> 00:37:08,363
They're going to separate us all out.

323
00:37:10,443 --> 00:37:12,003
They'll send her to Africa.

324
00:37:14,203 --> 00:37:15,443
Yeah?

325
00:37:16,196 --> 00:37:17,996
And where will they send you?

326
00:37:19,323 --> 00:37:20,843
Where will they send you, Karl?

327
00:37:22,003 --> 00:37:24,779
You're half Gypsy, so...

328
00:37:24,803 --> 00:37:26,203
...to Egypt maybe?

329
00:37:31,163 --> 00:37:33,979
Something I never told you before...

330
00:37:34,003 --> 00:37:35,763
...because it wasn't important.

331
00:37:37,363 --> 00:37:38,603
Maybe now, it is.

332
00:37:40,283 --> 00:37:41,963
Your dad was Jewish.

333
00:37:43,963 --> 00:37:47,099
He was the son of a tailor in Stechford.

334
00:37:47,123 --> 00:37:48,659
They changed their name to Thorne

335
00:37:48,683 --> 00:37:51,003
to stop the bricks coming through
the window.

336
00:37:53,356 --> 00:37:55,196
So, where will they send you, Karl?

337
00:37:58,483 --> 00:38:01,579
Mr Nelson, you can report back
to your President

338
00:38:01,603 --> 00:38:04,979
that the aristocracy and the
meritocracy are united

339
00:38:05,003 --> 00:38:08,043
in their conviction that a new order
is coming.

340
00:38:10,083 --> 00:38:14,619
Also, Mr Nelson, at present our
weapons are coming from Germany.

341
00:38:14,643 --> 00:38:17,059
The British are closing our supply
lines down.

342
00:38:17,083 --> 00:38:19,203
We would value a supply from Boston.

343
00:38:20,843 --> 00:38:24,299
Weapons, I can give you, if they're
to be used in a good cause.

344
00:38:24,323 --> 00:38:27,299
And while on the subject of import
and export,

345
00:38:27,323 --> 00:38:30,939
Mr Shelby, in light of our new
relationship,

346
00:38:30,963 --> 00:38:33,099
and since you have proven your
commitment

347
00:38:33,123 --> 00:38:35,539
in a most extraordinary way,

348
00:38:35,563 --> 00:38:39,683
Boston is now officially open for
the importation of your merchandise.

349
00:38:46,043 --> 00:38:47,243
Good.

350
00:39:28,363 --> 00:39:31,179
If we have established what we came
here to establish,

351
00:39:31,203 --> 00:39:32,979
perhaps we should all say goodnight.

352
00:39:33,003 --> 00:39:34,363
Absolutely.

353
00:40:21,843 --> 00:40:25,143
That's the same typewriter you
bought me all those years ago...

354
00:40:26,083 --> 00:40:28,143
...to help me become respectable.

355
00:40:29,349 --> 00:40:30,589
Do you remember?

356
00:40:32,163 --> 00:40:33,363
Yeah.

357
00:40:40,523 --> 00:40:42,003
This arrived.

358
00:40:43,003 --> 00:40:44,483
It's from the sanatorium.

359
00:40:46,083 --> 00:40:48,463
I've already paid Ruby's medical bills.

360
00:40:49,323 --> 00:40:51,259
I don't think it's a bill.

361
00:40:51,283 --> 00:40:54,143
It says it's urgent. It's from the
senior consultant.

362
00:41:13,123 --> 00:41:15,023
Why didn't you come to bed?

363
00:41:20,283 --> 00:41:22,243
Why didn't you come to bed?

364
00:41:28,002 --> 00:41:30,322
I'm typing up my recollection of the
meeting.

365
00:41:31,803 --> 00:41:36,763
If I... if I do it straight away, I
can quote people word for word.

366
00:41:38,443 --> 00:41:40,499
The information is more...

367
00:41:40,523 --> 00:41:43,223
...useful to Mr Churchill if it is
word for word.

368
00:42:10,769 --> 00:42:12,129
I burnt her chair.

369
00:42:14,443 --> 00:42:17,699
The paint on the wood left a smell
in the air.

370
00:42:17,983 --> 00:42:19,743
I didn't open the window.

371
00:42:22,163 --> 00:42:23,763
I quite like the smell.

372
00:42:49,523 --> 00:42:51,083
Not yet.

373
00:42:53,723 --> 00:42:55,123
Not yet.

374
00:42:57,643 --> 00:43:00,699
I have this work to do cos now I know...

375
00:43:00,723 --> 00:43:02,123
...that I will change.

376
00:43:04,363 --> 00:43:05,843
That I have to change.

377
00:43:07,603 --> 00:43:10,563
And change for good, Lizzie.

378
00:43:15,883 --> 00:43:17,163
Not just yet.

379
00:43:48,883 --> 00:43:50,003
Hello?

380
00:43:54,363 --> 00:43:55,643
Oh.

381
00:45:10,243 --> 00:45:11,823
I saw him leave.

382
00:45:13,563 --> 00:45:16,843
He keeps this apartment expressly
for this purpose, doesn't he?

383
00:45:18,883 --> 00:45:21,023
Are you following me, Mr Shelby?

384
00:45:21,923 --> 00:45:23,819
I'm flattered...

385
00:45:23,843 --> 00:45:25,263
...but why?

386
00:45:25,803 --> 00:45:27,419
When I do business with someone,

387
00:45:27,443 --> 00:45:30,203
I make it my business to know their
secrets.

388
00:45:33,016 --> 00:45:35,056
Mosley's reputation is no secret.

389
00:45:35,942 --> 00:45:37,062
Not him, you.

390
00:45:40,363 --> 00:45:42,303
How did you know I'd come here?

391
00:45:42,763 --> 00:45:44,563
I know things.

392
00:45:45,123 --> 00:45:47,483
I read people's minds, you know.

393
00:45:50,163 --> 00:45:53,459
Little glances across tables. It's a
gift.

394
00:45:53,483 --> 00:45:55,203
The whole family...

395
00:45:55,888 --> 00:45:57,688
...witches and sorcerers.

396
00:46:06,909 --> 00:46:08,429
Your uncle will disown you.

397
00:46:09,883 --> 00:46:12,763
Fucking his business partner behind
his back.

398
00:46:13,763 --> 00:46:15,459
You think he has morals?

399
00:46:15,483 --> 00:46:16,739
He's a Catholic.

400
00:46:16,763 --> 00:46:19,503
Men do what they want, women do what
they are told.

401
00:46:21,363 --> 00:46:22,803
Will you tell Michael?

402
00:46:24,083 --> 00:46:25,403
Michael is family.

403
00:46:26,996 --> 00:46:28,516
We are a family healed.

404
00:46:30,323 --> 00:46:32,419
You have no interest in me...

405
00:46:32,622 --> 00:46:33,862
...or in Michael.

406
00:46:35,803 --> 00:46:38,243
So, why don't you just tell me what
you actually want?

407
00:46:50,363 --> 00:46:52,979
You will be with Mosley...

408
00:46:53,149 --> 00:46:54,549
...when he's in Berlin.

409
00:46:55,563 --> 00:46:56,699
You'll be in the room,

410
00:46:56,723 --> 00:46:59,539
when he meets senior members of the
German Government.

411
00:46:59,563 --> 00:47:01,883
I want to know what is discussed...

412
00:47:02,923 --> 00:47:04,763
...and I want to know what is decided.

413
00:47:07,443 --> 00:47:08,523
And if I lie?

414
00:47:10,843 --> 00:47:12,283
I will know.

415
00:47:21,383 --> 00:47:23,503
You know Michael thinks you're the
devil...

416
00:47:25,109 --> 00:47:27,189
...and I think he might actually be
right.

417
00:47:28,843 --> 00:47:30,983
That was the other reason I came here.

418
00:47:31,443 --> 00:47:35,299
What are Michael's real intentions
toward me, Gina?

419
00:47:35,523 --> 00:47:37,343
And if you lie, I will know.

420
00:47:42,649 --> 00:47:43,809
Tommy...

421
00:47:45,163 --> 00:47:47,423
...he intends to complete the deal.

422
00:47:48,563 --> 00:47:50,163
And then, you both walk away.

423
00:48:04,603 --> 00:48:06,003
Fuck.

424
00:49:28,123 --> 00:49:29,363
Come.

425
00:49:31,763 --> 00:49:33,603
Mr Shelby, Doctor Holford.

426
00:49:36,723 --> 00:49:37,923
Send him in.

427
00:49:45,483 --> 00:49:47,499
You said it had to be in person.

428
00:49:47,689 --> 00:49:48,929
Here I am.

429
00:49:50,643 --> 00:49:52,443
You might want to sit down.

430
00:49:59,643 --> 00:50:02,983
Mr Shelby, I know that you are still
grieving for your daughter...

431
00:50:04,403 --> 00:50:06,483
...but I have news that cannot wait.

432
00:50:11,323 --> 00:50:16,703
When you were X-rayed and examined
at the sanatorium ten days ago...

433
00:50:18,683 --> 00:50:21,963
...there was no TB found in your lung.

434
00:50:24,003 --> 00:50:27,099
But I am afraid they found something
else.

435
00:50:27,303 --> 00:50:29,743
Something related to your daughter's
illness.

436
00:50:33,403 --> 00:50:36,419
They tried to speak to you at the
hospital

437
00:50:36,443 --> 00:50:38,083
but you were not co-operating.

438
00:50:39,603 --> 00:50:41,523
After your daughter's death,

439
00:50:42,403 --> 00:50:45,743
you could not be found to be
informed in person.

440
00:50:46,243 --> 00:50:49,743
Eventually, as your personal doctor,
they called me.

441
00:50:52,883 --> 00:50:55,843
I didn't offer you tea. You look
like death. Do you want tea?

442
00:50:57,683 --> 00:50:58,843
No.

443
00:51:00,563 --> 00:51:03,463
At the sanatorium, they conducted
blood tests.

444
00:51:05,323 --> 00:51:09,019
The tests suggest that the shadow
you can see

445
00:51:09,043 --> 00:51:11,179
at the base of your skull...

446
00:51:11,203 --> 00:51:12,803
...is not cancer.

447
00:51:14,003 --> 00:51:15,563
It is tuberculoma.

448
00:51:18,123 --> 00:51:21,843
A tubercular growth caused by the
same bacteria as TB.

449
00:51:25,203 --> 00:51:27,443
You may have picked it up from your
daughter.

450
00:51:29,243 --> 00:51:33,419
Once this disease enters a
household, it can run wild.

451
00:51:33,443 --> 00:51:36,243
It can be transmitted with a simple
kiss.

452
00:51:40,203 --> 00:51:42,803
It seems the Shelby household is no
exception.

453
00:51:46,883 --> 00:51:51,123
Mr Shelby, as I say, I am aware that
you are still grieving...

454
00:51:52,323 --> 00:51:55,023
...but you must understand this is
very serious.

455
00:51:57,003 --> 00:52:00,483
From the size of the tumour,
expansion must've been rapid.

456
00:52:01,683 --> 00:52:05,443
I have no doubt that you are already
experiencing symptoms?

457
00:52:07,123 --> 00:52:09,123
Have you recently suffered seizures?

458
00:52:10,523 --> 00:52:16,463
Bouts of weakness, dissociation,
hallucinations?

459
00:52:24,123 --> 00:52:25,883
Why didn't you come and see me?

460
00:52:28,443 --> 00:52:29,923
I have work to do.

461
00:52:33,603 --> 00:52:35,083
Am I a danger to others?

462
00:52:36,883 --> 00:52:38,163
No.

463
00:52:38,563 --> 00:52:42,179
Unlike TB, tuberculoma is not
infectious.

464
00:52:42,383 --> 00:52:46,339
Mr Shelby, it is not infectious...

465
00:52:46,363 --> 00:52:48,143
...but in your case...

466
00:52:48,723 --> 00:52:50,843
...I am afraid it is inoperable.

467
00:52:52,643 --> 00:52:54,579
The growth is in your brain stem.

468
00:52:54,603 --> 00:52:55,979
Any attempt to remove it

469
00:52:56,003 --> 00:52:58,743
would result in trauma and brain
haemorrhage.

470
00:53:03,163 --> 00:53:04,979
Whilst you were refusing my calls,

471
00:53:05,003 --> 00:53:08,363
I showed your X-rays to three of
the best surgeons in the country.

472
00:53:12,283 --> 00:53:14,343
They all said they would not operate...

473
00:53:15,523 --> 00:53:16,883
...as it would be futile.

474
00:53:18,563 --> 00:53:22,843
Of course, you will want a second
opinion for yourself.

475
00:53:24,043 --> 00:53:27,219
Doctor Helen Rutherford at St Thomas'.

476
00:53:27,243 --> 00:53:28,563
She is a friend.

477
00:53:39,843 --> 00:53:41,283
This...

478
00:53:43,123 --> 00:53:44,483
How bad will it get?

479
00:53:50,883 --> 00:53:53,099
As the tumour grows,

480
00:53:53,256 --> 00:53:57,096
the rate of physical and mental
deterioration will increase.

481
00:54:01,603 --> 00:54:06,299
Eventually, you will need people
around you constantly,

482
00:54:06,323 --> 00:54:08,043
who love you very much.

483
00:54:11,509 --> 00:54:12,749
How long?

484
00:54:16,243 --> 00:54:19,743
I understand you have defeated many
enemies, Mr Shelby.

485
00:54:20,763 --> 00:54:22,979
Now, you have a new one...

486
00:54:23,003 --> 00:54:24,283
...inside you.

487
00:54:25,763 --> 00:54:27,203
You cannot defeat it...

488
00:54:28,643 --> 00:54:30,843
...but you can keep it at bay for a
while.

489
00:54:31,363 --> 00:54:35,579
If you live correctly, if you are
determined and if you fight...

490
00:54:35,603 --> 00:54:37,539
I asked you a question.

491
00:54:37,563 --> 00:54:39,179
So, I want an answer.

492
00:54:39,203 --> 00:54:42,019
I don't want your fucking platitudes.

493
00:54:42,043 --> 00:54:46,783
How long before I need people around
me, who love me very much?

494
00:54:51,443 --> 00:54:53,299
- Sorry.
- It's fine, Lizzie.

495
00:54:53,323 --> 00:54:55,383
My accountant here was just leaving.

496
00:55:00,883 --> 00:55:03,379
I will telephone you, when I get
back to London.

497
00:55:03,403 --> 00:55:04,859
No, I don't have enough time.

498
00:55:04,883 --> 00:55:07,563
You're an accountant, give me a
fucking number now.

499
00:55:08,883 --> 00:55:10,463
One year.

500
00:55:11,403 --> 00:55:13,619
Perhaps 18 months.

501
00:55:13,643 --> 00:55:16,139
That's fine. That's all I need to know.

502
00:55:16,163 --> 00:55:19,443
I will adjust my finances
accordingly. Thank you.

503
00:55:21,523 --> 00:55:23,268
I will write to you,
explaining the full implications.

504
00:55:23,292 --> 00:55:25,163
Yeah, thank you.

505
00:55:29,229 --> 00:55:30,909
Good day.

506
00:55:38,923 --> 00:55:40,863
Something serious?

507
00:55:41,483 --> 00:55:43,699
No, no, just a...

508
00:55:44,229 --> 00:55:47,899
...just a bill I wasn't expecting and
I...

509
00:55:47,923 --> 00:55:49,523
I'll have to pay it.

510
00:55:59,403 --> 00:56:01,523
Will you give me a minute on my own,
Lizzie?

511
00:56:05,543 --> 00:56:06,903
Yeah.

512
00:56:22,443 --> 00:56:23,763
Not a devil...

513
00:56:26,843 --> 00:56:28,763
...just an ordinary mortal man.

514
00:56:35,283 --> 00:56:37,563
There will be a war in this family...

515
00:56:39,803 --> 00:56:41,643
...and one of you will die.

516
00:56:44,043 --> 00:56:45,563
Polly.

517
00:56:47,363 --> 00:56:49,963
Just give me enough time to do what
I have to do.

518
00:56:52,123 --> 00:56:53,539
Kill.

519
00:56:53,563 --> 00:56:55,323
Kill.

1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:04,162

00:00:01,500 --> 00:00:03,311

2
00:00:03,335 --> 00:00:07,575

3
00:00:07,644 --> 00:00:10,620
Jack says just a few more weeks and

4
00:00:10,644 --> 00:00:12,860
Stories about you come up the canal.

5
00:00:12,884 --> 00:00:16,180
Once you walked fine alone,
now you need a stick.

6
00:00:16,204 --> 00:00:18,300
You stay clean for two weeks,

7
00:00:18,324 --> 00:00:19,980

8
00:00:20,004 --> 00:00:22,180
Have you recently suffered seizures?

9
00:00:22,204 --> 00:00:25,004
It is Tuberculoma, I am
afraid it is inoperable.

10
00:01:47,724 --> 00:01:49,380
Mr Shelby.

11
00:01:49,404 --> 00:01:51,780
I only gave opium to your brother

12
00:01:51,804 --> 00:01:53,540
because he give me big trouble.

13
00:01:53,564 --> 00:01:55,244
He attacked my wife.

14
00:02:03,004 --> 00:02:05,884
I would like a pot of green tea, please.

15
00:02:17,564 --> 00:02:19,820
It has taken me ten years
to build this business.

16
00:02:19,844 --> 00:02:22,604
Your business will be safe,
if you do what I say.

17
00:02:26,404 --> 00:02:28,484
How much opium do you have in
your cellar?

18
00:02:30,044 --> 00:02:31,580
Five pounds.

19
00:02:32,164 --> 00:02:33,564
Bring it to me.

20
00:02:35,164 --> 00:02:37,724
Four minutes against the clock.

21
00:03:09,516 --> 00:03:11,476
As member of Parliament...

22
00:03:13,997 --> 00:03:16,100
...for this constituency...

23
00:03:16,730 --> 00:03:19,226
...it is my duty to take
responsibility for the welfare

24
00:03:19,324 --> 00:03:21,900
- of my constituents.
- Mr Shelby, the clock is still ticking.

25
00:03:21,924 --> 00:03:26,060
The consumption of opium is very
prejudicial to health.

26
00:03:26,084 --> 00:03:28,180
Women give it to their children
so they can leave

27
00:03:28,204 --> 00:03:30,700

in the factories.

28
00:03:30,724 --> 00:03:33,324
Men lose their jobs when they
become addicted.

29
00:03:35,144 --> 00:03:37,760
From now on, you will sell

30
00:03:37,844 --> 00:03:41,444

31
00:03:42,571 --> 00:03:45,227
If I hear that you are selling
opium again,

32
00:03:45,251 --> 00:03:48,107

quickly for you. Do you understand?

33
00:03:48,131 --> 00:03:50,747
Yes, I understand, I will stop.

34
00:03:50,771 --> 00:03:52,771
Mr Shelby, the clock is still ticking.

35
00:03:53,600 --> 00:03:55,600
_

36
00:03:59,571 --> 00:04:01,740
Please tell...

37
00:04:02,251 --> 00:04:05,460

38
00:04:05,851 --> 00:04:07,660
...that from now on...

39
00:04:08,051 --> 00:04:11,187
...there will be no more opium...

40
00:04:11,211 --> 00:04:15,180
...in Small Heath or in Bordesley.

41
00:04:15,691 --> 00:04:17,371
Thank you for the tea.

42
00:04:28,488 --> 00:04:29,660
_

43
00:04:30,032 --> 00:04:33,040
_

44

45
00:04:57,131 --> 00:04:58,891
Yes, sir, Mr Shelby.

46
00:05:00,891 --> 00:05:04,427
You tell the pub and cafe owners
in Montague Street...

47

48
00:05:06,571 --> 00:05:08,387

49
00:05:08,411 --> 00:05:10,587

50

District Council.

51
00:05:15,756 --> 00:05:20,615
Synced & corrected by -robtor-

52

Sorry I'm late, they closed Montague
Street.

53
00:05:30,691 --> 00:05:33,051
There's a gas explosion or...

54
00:05:37,891 --> 00:05:39,907
Right. Well, it would be nice if
just one thing

55
00:05:39,931 --> 00:05:42,491
could happen in Birmingham that
wasn't our fault.

56
00:05:47,171 --> 00:05:50,467
I have gathered you all here today
because there is news

57
00:05:50,491 --> 00:05:52,731
and it is of interest to the whole
family.

58
00:05:54,051 --> 00:05:55,827
First of all,

59
00:05:55,851 --> 00:05:57,463
I would like to welcome

60
00:05:57,487 --> 00:06:01,371
Finn's new wife Mary to the family.

61
00:06:03,051 --> 00:06:07,467
Right. Well, I'm very glad I dragged
myself out of bed for this.

62
00:06:07,491 --> 00:06:09,267
There is...

63
00:06:09,291 --> 00:06:11,147
...one more item of business.

64
00:06:11,171 --> 00:06:12,267
Johnny.

65
00:06:12,291 --> 00:06:13,811
Tom.

66
00:06:15,051 --> 00:06:17,731
Come on, come on, hurry up.

67
00:06:24,371 --> 00:06:26,180
Everyone...

68
00:06:27,291 --> 00:06:29,940
...this here is Erasmus.

69
00:06:30,451 --> 00:06:32,220
Nobody calls me that.

70
00:06:32,771 --> 00:06:34,740
They call him Duke.

71
00:06:37,171 --> 00:06:41,227
20 years ago, at Apple by horse fair...

72
00:06:41,251 --> 00:06:42,627
...I met a girl.

73
00:06:42,651 --> 00:06:44,651
We shared the shade of a hazel tree.

74
00:06:45,731 --> 00:06:48,731
Nine months later this lad was born.

75
00:06:51,651 --> 00:06:53,260
This is my son.

76
00:06:53,891 --> 00:06:56,307
His mother died on the road.

77
00:06:56,331 --> 00:06:58,667
Up until now I never tried to find him.

78
00:06:58,691 --> 00:07:02,900
But I am trying to look at life in a
different way.

79
00:07:04,771 --> 00:07:06,900
A child is a precious thing.

80
00:07:09,251 --> 00:07:10,627
So I am bringing him...

81
00:07:10,651 --> 00:07:13,027
Into the fucking family with
a snap of his fingers.

82
00:07:13,051 --> 00:07:16,307
No, I am bringing him into the fold.

83
00:07:16,331 --> 00:07:18,700
He'll have to earn membership of
the family.

84
00:07:19,691 --> 00:07:21,987
For the moment, welcome, son.
You have a seat.

85
00:07:22,011 --> 00:07:23,771
Go on, sit down here.

86
00:07:30,211 --> 00:07:32,220
There are some mistakes I've made...

87
00:07:32,851 --> 00:07:34,620
...that I can never address...

88
00:07:35,477 --> 00:07:36,797
...and some I can.

89
00:07:37,771 --> 00:07:39,587
Some wounds I can try to heal.

90
00:07:39,611 --> 00:07:41,811
And new wounds you can open up.

91
00:07:43,331 --> 00:07:44,531
Anyway...

92
00:07:45,731 --> 00:07:47,907
...that's the business of the day.

93
00:07:47,931 --> 00:07:49,931
Is it too early for whisky?

94
00:07:57,011 --> 00:07:58,580
There you go.

95
00:07:59,171 --> 00:08:01,667
Shelby breakfast for you, son.

96
00:08:01,691 --> 00:08:03,300
I don't drink.

97
00:08:03,771 --> 00:08:05,467
And I'm not a Shelby, all right?

98
00:08:05,491 --> 00:08:07,100
I'm a Duke.

99
00:08:07,891 --> 00:08:09,267
Ooh, hoo, hoo, hoo.

100
00:08:09,291 --> 00:08:10,787
You're a fucking Shelby, all right,

101
00:08:10,811 --> 00:08:12,500
don't worry about that.

102
00:08:13,011 --> 00:08:15,827
Mm, I think we will need Curly

103
00:08:15,851 --> 00:08:18,387
and a strong rope to break this one
in, Tom.

104
00:08:18,411 --> 00:08:20,507
Arthur, open up the shop,

105
00:08:20,531 --> 00:08:23,427
put the kid here on the blackboard,
writing up the odds.

106
00:08:23,451 --> 00:08:25,060
I can't write.

107
00:08:25,971 --> 00:08:28,491
Put the kid on the blackboard,
wiping off the chalk.

108
00:08:31,491 --> 00:08:33,267
Go on, son.

109
00:08:33,291 --> 00:08:35,011
Come on then.

110
00:08:52,811 --> 00:08:55,851
Lizzie, come on.

111
00:09:02,211 --> 00:09:04,547
My father was the Duke of the Saxon
Shore.

112
00:09:04,571 --> 00:09:06,387
My mother was a Romany Queen.

113
00:09:06,411 --> 00:09:08,660
Who told you that, your mum?

114
00:09:09,091 --> 00:09:11,780
I don't allow people to talk about
my mother.

115
00:09:14,091 --> 00:09:15,747
Good for you.

116
00:09:15,771 --> 00:09:18,467
So let's get this right then,
you can't read,

117
00:09:18,491 --> 00:09:20,867
you can't fucking write,
there's nothing wrong with that.

118
00:09:20,891 --> 00:09:23,307
What can you do, eh?

119
00:09:23,331 --> 00:09:25,187
I can tell the time.

120
00:09:25,211 --> 00:09:26,587
You can tell the time.

121
00:09:26,611 --> 00:09:28,787
Here, he can tell the time.

122
00:09:28,811 --> 00:09:30,371
Ain't that clever.

123
00:09:31,651 --> 00:09:34,091
It's a lot more than you can fucking do.

124
00:09:36,571 --> 00:09:38,771
What did you just say to me?

125
00:09:39,891 --> 00:09:41,931
What time is it, Mr Shelby?

126
00:09:45,731 --> 00:09:47,427
That's what I can do.

127
00:09:47,451 --> 00:09:50,451
You little bastard.

128
00:09:51,731 --> 00:09:53,987
Here, keep it.

129
00:09:54,011 --> 00:09:56,171
Stop you from being late in the future.

130
00:10:23,891 --> 00:10:27,171
Is there forgiveness in your heart
for Arthur Shelby?

131
00:10:28,451 --> 00:10:29,820
No.

132
00:10:33,171 --> 00:10:35,571
But maybe there will be forgiveness
from God.

133
00:10:38,131 --> 00:10:40,587
And you will do God's work?

134
00:10:40,611 --> 00:10:43,467
God is interested in you as well, Tommy.

135
00:10:43,491 --> 00:10:47,260
And God will be with you on your
journey every step of the way.

136
00:10:50,891 --> 00:10:53,091
He may not need to take many steps.

137
00:11:07,211 --> 00:11:08,611
Tell me this, Linda...

138
00:11:10,411 --> 00:11:13,180
...is God interested in me...

139
00:11:13,810 --> 00:11:15,530
...or in my money?

140
00:11:20,051 --> 00:11:22,107
I believe you run a foundation

141
00:11:22,131 --> 00:11:25,427
and that your foundation has many
missions across the world

142
00:11:25,451 --> 00:11:27,507
but in these times of financial crisis,

143
00:11:27,531 --> 00:11:29,507
funding is hard to come by.

144
00:11:29,531 --> 00:11:33,347
So perhaps your God's plan is
a practical one.

145
00:11:33,371 --> 00:11:36,747
Perhaps he would like me to make
a donation

146
00:11:36,771 --> 00:11:39,708
to your foundation, and in return,

147
00:11:40,200 --> 00:11:42,107
he would like you

148
00:11:42,131 --> 00:11:45,220
to help my brother on his road
to redemption.

149
00:11:45,651 --> 00:11:47,987
Now, I know that in a place of
worship such as this,

150
00:11:48,011 --> 00:11:50,227
you would never ask how much.

151
00:11:50,251 --> 00:11:52,380
So I will tell you plainly.

152
00:11:52,811 --> 00:11:56,147
I will write your foundation
a cheque for £10,000...

153
00:11:56,620 --> 00:11:58,507
Praise the Lord.

154
00:11:58,531 --> 00:12:01,291
...if you agree to look kindly on
Arthur and to help him.

155
00:12:04,331 --> 00:12:07,140
I need to look after everyone in
the family.

156
00:12:09,324 --> 00:12:11,004
Do we have a deal?

157
00:12:13,771 --> 00:12:16,780
Your money will be spent to do good
around the world.

158
00:12:17,871 --> 00:12:19,951
And a mission will be named after you.

159
00:12:23,171 --> 00:12:25,180
But I am only agreeing to help him...

160
00:12:25,811 --> 00:12:27,460
...not sleep with him.

161
00:12:27,891 --> 00:12:29,300
No.

162
00:12:30,171 --> 00:12:33,027
Now, I imagine the negotiation for
that particular favour

163
00:12:33,051 --> 00:12:35,620
would take a considerable amount of
time...

164
00:12:36,851 --> 00:12:38,771
...and I have an appointment.

165
00:12:40,470 --> 00:12:42,230
God bless.

166
00:13:04,811 --> 00:13:07,531
Apologies for the initial
misunderstanding.

167
00:13:09,171 --> 00:13:11,371
My brother dealt with it.

168
00:13:17,531 --> 00:13:19,531
For the care you took.

169
00:13:21,211 --> 00:13:23,987
Even though I succumbed to temptation.

170
00:13:24,011 --> 00:13:26,827
Part of the reason my brother is
back dealing with it,

171
00:13:26,851 --> 00:13:29,667
is down to you, you spoke to him.

172
00:13:29,691 --> 00:13:31,107
As a comrade.

173
00:13:31,131 --> 00:13:32,728
The beating is still owed to you.

174
00:13:32,753 --> 00:13:34,289
Do you still do that kind of work

175
00:13:34,314 --> 00:13:36,520
yourself, Thomas Shelby, MP?

176
00:13:37,371 --> 00:13:41,091
Mr Stagg, see, I can use men like you.

177
00:13:43,571 --> 00:13:46,580
I have friends that are in need of guns.

178
00:13:47,971 --> 00:13:49,747
Soon, there will be a shipment

179
00:13:49,771 --> 00:13:54,507
of Thompson sub machine guns
coming here from Boston.

180
00:13:54,850 --> 00:13:57,850
And I need you to unload
and store those weapons.

181
00:14:00,144 --> 00:14:02,584
There will also be ammunition...

182
00:14:03,250 --> 00:14:04,450
...like this.

183
00:14:05,820 --> 00:14:07,907
You have a good look.

184
00:14:07,931 --> 00:14:12,027
And I need you to take better care
of the guns and ammunition

185
00:14:12,157 --> 00:14:13,757
than you did of the powder.

186
00:14:15,037 --> 00:14:16,077
You understand?

187
00:14:17,340 --> 00:14:19,027
Previously,

188
00:14:19,540 --> 00:14:23,747
all of my import and export
went through Belfast docks.

189
00:14:23,771 --> 00:14:25,411
Now we're dealing with Boston...

190
00:14:28,277 --> 00:14:32,277
...I am considering shifting
my supply line to Liverpool.

191
00:14:33,331 --> 00:14:34,940
You'll be a very rich man.

192
00:14:38,797 --> 00:14:40,620
Don't you ever say thank you?

193
00:14:59,097 --> 00:15:00,417
Thank you.

194
00:15:04,931 --> 00:15:06,611
Is that why you do it, Mr Shelby?

195
00:15:08,411 --> 00:15:10,707
Is that why you keep all this going?

196
00:15:10,731 --> 00:15:12,771
To have people say thank you?

197
00:15:14,291 --> 00:15:16,427
You could close all this down.

198
00:15:16,451 --> 00:15:18,827
You could leave the sport behind.

199
00:15:18,851 --> 00:15:22,267
You could live like
an ordinary mortal man.

200
00:15:22,291 --> 00:15:24,280
On your gravestone,

201
00:15:24,731 --> 00:15:26,540
"an ordinary mortal man".

202
00:15:28,131 --> 00:15:29,747
But, instead,

203
00:15:29,771 --> 00:15:33,267
you still go round collecting
"please" and "thank you"

204
00:15:33,291 --> 00:15:36,411
and "sorry" and "forgive me, Mr Shelby."

205
00:15:38,404 --> 00:15:39,764

00:35:53,971 --> 00:35:57,827
The watch had the words
"Saxon Shore" carved in it.

472
00:35:57,851 --> 00:36:00,820
I stole it myself
from a drunk when I was a kid.

473
00:36:02,131 --> 00:36:03,187
I imagine she told you

474
00:36:03,211 --> 00:36:05,187
your dad was
the Duke of the Saxon Shore.

475
00:36:05,211 --> 00:36:06,867
Well...

476
00:36:07,420 --> 00:36:09,027
...I am the Duke,

477
00:36:09,051 --> 00:36:10,660
it was my watch.

478
00:36:11,131 --> 00:36:12,331
I am your father.

479
00:36:14,891 --> 00:36:15,931
That's the truth.

480
00:36:17,171 --> 00:36:18,347
When her dad found out,

481
00:36:18,371 --> 00:36:20,091
he shot me in the chest
with a squirrel gun.

482
00:36:21,851 --> 00:36:26,931
A scar and a stolen watch
and a story she made up.

483
00:36:28,651 --> 00:36:30,387
That's all you need to know
about yourself

484
00:36:30,411 --> 00:36:31,931
before you get on the road.

485
00:36:44,691 --> 00:36:46,731
Esme told me the spirits favour you.

486
00:36:48,740 --> 00:36:50,307
That the spirit is in you.

487
00:36:50,700 --> 00:36:53,011
She tried to sell me like one
of those horses, didn't she?

488
00:36:54,051 --> 00:36:56,347
How much did she pay for me?

489
00:36:57,540 --> 00:36:59,867
I have no use for gold any more.

490
00:36:59,891 --> 00:37:01,827
But if you're a horse,

491
00:37:02,363 --> 00:37:04,123
you're in the right place.

492
00:37:05,150 --> 00:37:06,270
Curly!

493
00:37:08,451 --> 00:37:10,180
Curly. Hurry up.

494
00:37:10,971 --> 00:37:12,691
This boy has hills to climb.

495
00:37:15,997 --> 00:37:17,277
I remember that watch.

496
00:37:19,810 --> 00:37:21,370
Oh, yeah?

497
00:37:22,651 --> 00:37:24,411
She used to wear it over her heart.

498
00:37:27,804 --> 00:37:29,460
We buried it with her.

499
00:37:32,811 --> 00:37:36,387
Tom. The old wagon's
right front wheel is fucked, Tom.

500
00:37:36,411 --> 00:37:37,731
It's standing in the wet.

501
00:37:39,051 --> 00:37:40,331
Put a new one on, Curly.

502
00:37:43,343 --> 00:37:44,743
Yeah.

503
00:37:47,210 --> 00:37:48,650
They fix wagons here.

504
00:37:50,211 --> 00:37:52,907
Good families come from the New Forest

505
00:37:52,931 --> 00:37:54,907
to have their wagons fixed

506
00:37:55,170 --> 00:37:57,370
and get fresh horses before the fairs.

507
00:38:00,523 --> 00:38:02,963
Yeah. Yeah, I like it here.

508
00:38:04,051 --> 00:38:05,811
I like it better than that betting shop.

509
00:38:08,771 --> 00:38:10,180
Why?

510
00:38:10,851 --> 00:38:12,180
People.

511
00:38:12,940 --> 00:38:14,380
People piss me off.

512
00:38:16,371 --> 00:38:18,291
There are a lot of people
in that betting shop.

513
00:38:19,931 --> 00:38:22,507
So far, here I've only counted two.

514
00:38:22,531 --> 00:38:23,860
Uh-huh.

515
00:38:24,251 --> 00:38:25,547
Charlie and Curly,

516
00:38:25,571 --> 00:38:27,387
the rest is dogs and horses.

517
00:38:27,411 --> 00:38:29,220
Curly's half horse himself.

518
00:38:30,643 --> 00:38:31,923
Dogs are OK.

519
00:38:32,891 --> 00:38:34,691
Horses are better than people, mind you.

520
00:38:38,317 --> 00:38:40,757
There's work here
for a man who knows horses.

521
00:38:44,171 --> 00:38:45,371
Unknown.

522
00:38:46,571 --> 00:38:48,540
I want to remain completely unknown.

523
00:38:49,291 --> 00:38:51,307
Well, you'd be in the right place
for that as well.

524
00:38:51,331 --> 00:38:52,491
No-one knows anyone here.

525
00:38:54,531 --> 00:38:56,611
Hey, mister. Save that wheel a minute.

526
00:38:58,731 --> 00:38:59,971
Where would I stay?

527
00:39:01,651 --> 00:39:04,980
Stables, with the other stallions.

528
00:39:05,971 --> 00:39:07,947
Now that Finn is married off,

529
00:39:07,971 --> 00:39:09,987
there are plenty of girls round here.

530
00:39:10,304 --> 00:39:13,464
Their fathers are mostly unarmed.

531
00:39:17,164 --> 00:39:19,484
I have a future for you, Duke.

532
00:39:21,611 --> 00:39:22,851
You already have a son.

533
00:39:25,037 --> 00:39:26,597
My business has two sides.

534
00:39:27,731 --> 00:39:29,091
Light and dark.

535
00:39:30,197 --> 00:39:32,060
I'll need someone for each.

536
00:39:33,091 --> 00:39:35,100
And I'm dark, am I?

537
00:39:36,524 --> 00:39:39,204
I have realised we don't get
to choose which one we are.

538
00:39:40,863 --> 00:39:42,063
Dark knows dark.

539
00:39:43,737 --> 00:39:46,097
And my affairs, both light and dark...

540
00:39:47,390 --> 00:39:48,990
...will need settling soon.

541
00:39:50,980 --> 00:39:56,187
Curly? Find a shovel for
the Duke of the Saxon Shore here.

542
00:39:56,700 --> 00:39:58,027
Get him shovelling shit.

543
00:39:59,411 --> 00:40:01,347
And put some petrol in the boat.

544
00:40:01,577 --> 00:40:03,617
I'm off to meet a lady in Solihull.

545
00:40:43,131 --> 00:40:44,291
Take a look at her.

546
00:40:45,943 --> 00:40:48,943
Now imagine ten people living on side.

547
00:40:50,890 --> 00:40:52,450
Step on. Have a look inside.

548
00:40:58,411 --> 00:41:01,387
I've had a response
from the Guinness Trust

549
00:41:01,411 --> 00:41:05,547
about building charitable housing
at two sites

550
00:41:05,571 --> 00:41:09,427
along the canal network between London,

551
00:41:09,451 --> 00:41:11,187
Birmingham and Liverpool.

552
00:41:11,740 --> 00:41:15,100
This lock here would be
the one of the sites.

553
00:41:16,131 --> 00:41:19,540
I have the permission.
We just need the finance.

554
00:41:21,611 --> 00:41:24,987
I know that you and your husband,
Bryan Guinness, are estranged,

555
00:41:25,011 --> 00:41:27,667
but I understand
you still have influence

556
00:41:27,691 --> 00:41:29,500
in the Guinness family.

557
00:41:29,931 --> 00:41:32,667
Your support might help them
make their decision.

558
00:41:32,691 --> 00:41:34,131
Will you help me?

559
00:41:43,811 --> 00:41:46,056
I've booked a suite in a hotel
a mile from here.

560
00:41:47,411 --> 00:41:48,971
My chauffeur will take us there.

561
00:41:51,051 --> 00:41:52,907
You look quite the thing
dressed like that,

562
00:41:52,931 --> 00:41:54,707
dressed like a working man.

563
00:41:54,731 --> 00:41:56,547
They'll probably show you
to the coal house

564
00:41:56,571 --> 00:41:58,627
to make your delivery.

565
00:41:58,984 --> 00:42:01,384
Yep, they probably will.

566
00:42:04,297 --> 00:42:06,353
Oswald has fucked your wife,

567
00:42:06,437 --> 00:42:09,277
so my suggestion is
about balance and proportion.

568
00:42:10,190 --> 00:42:11,430
It would be only fair.

569
00:42:15,404 --> 00:42:16,684
Can I assume...

570
00:42:17,770 --> 00:42:19,170
...I have your support?

571
00:42:23,171 --> 00:42:27,307
This isn't about charitable housing,
this is about changing the world.

572
00:42:27,331 --> 00:42:30,147
It's about a different kind of trust.

573
00:42:30,171 --> 00:42:31,611
Absolute trust.

574
00:42:32,851 --> 00:42:34,651
We have important work ahead of us.

575
00:42:37,340 --> 00:42:38,547
It's much harder to lie

576
00:42:38,571 --> 00:42:40,131
with your body than with your words.

577
00:42:41,637 --> 00:42:42,917
This, I have learnt.

578
00:42:50,931 --> 00:42:52,940
Mostly, I do whatever I want to do.

579
00:42:54,051 --> 00:42:56,667
Sometimes, I do things for the cause.

580
00:42:56,691 --> 00:42:58,620
In this case, it's both.

581
00:43:01,711 --> 00:43:02,951
Come.

582
00:43:29,171 --> 00:43:31,267
In the interests of absolute clarity,

583
00:43:31,291 --> 00:43:32,867
that is simply

584
00:43:32,891 --> 00:43:35,620
the English aristocracy's way
of shaking hands.

585
00:43:39,370 --> 00:43:40,610
So...

586
00:43:41,263 --> 00:43:42,660
Welcome.

587
00:46:27,451 --> 00:46:29,251
If you do this thing...

588
00:46:30,851 --> 00:46:34,411
...the possibility of war,
you have to consider.

589
00:46:40,011 --> 00:46:41,347
It was the ambitions

590
00:46:41,371 --> 00:46:43,371
and strategies of one man
that caused this.

591
00:46:47,251 --> 00:46:50,467
There will be a war in this family.

592
00:46:50,491 --> 00:46:52,667
And one of you will die.

593
00:47:18,131 --> 00:47:21,827
We need to leave early to catch
the first train to Liverpool, yes?

594
00:47:21,851 --> 00:47:23,347
Yep.

595
00:47:23,637 --> 00:47:25,917
So eat early, finish early.

596
00:47:30,811 --> 00:47:32,700
You changed the combination of the safe.

597
00:47:34,178 --> 00:47:35,498
Why?

598
00:47:36,051 --> 00:47:37,700
Have you got new secrets?

599
00:47:38,571 --> 00:47:40,987
With the new business at hand,

600
00:47:41,540 --> 00:47:44,067
there are some things

601
00:47:44,091 --> 00:47:45,787
that I cannot share.

602
00:47:45,811 --> 00:47:47,540
What things?

603
00:47:53,051 --> 00:47:54,507
What are those tablets?

604
00:47:55,020 --> 00:47:56,427
The doctor gave them me.

605
00:47:56,451 --> 00:47:57,987
Pain killers?

606
00:47:58,011 --> 00:48:00,500
- Yeah.
- What pain?

607
00:48:01,417 --> 00:48:03,457
Any pain that comes, Lizzie.

608
00:48:26,583 --> 00:48:29,359
When you're ready, I want you
to tell me everything

609
00:48:29,384 --> 00:48:30,624
that's going on.

610
00:48:33,371 --> 00:48:35,267
It's like the clock's stopped ticking

611
00:48:35,291 --> 00:48:37,411
and I'm waiting for the bomb to explode.

612
00:48:41,817 --> 00:48:43,617
We are in that quiet minute.

613
00:48:50,191 --> 00:48:51,671
Tommy?

614
00:48:59,750 --> 00:49:01,790
That's where we live now.

615
00:49:03,697 --> 00:49:05,337
When I know everything...

616
00:49:07,004 --> 00:49:08,844
...I will tell you everything.

617
00:49:25,531 --> 00:49:27,587
Oh, no, Gina's running wild, y'see.

618
00:49:27,611 --> 00:49:30,267
Harrods, dope, amphetamines,
lords and ladies,

619
00:49:30,291 --> 00:49:32,307
you know, the whole
English aristocracy thing.

620
00:49:32,331 --> 00:49:34,067
Fuck wine, whiskey.

621
00:49:34,700 --> 00:49:36,107
Shelby, you having whiskey?

622
00:49:36,131 --> 00:49:37,347
I'll stay on wine.

623
00:49:37,371 --> 00:49:40,467
Fuck wine, more whiskey.
I'm celebrating.

624
00:49:40,491 --> 00:49:43,827
Celebration, you know.
Getting off this fucking island.

625
00:49:43,851 --> 00:49:45,267
You see, the thing with England,

626
00:49:45,291 --> 00:49:47,707
the currency here, it's not money.

627
00:49:47,731 --> 00:49:50,620
Nah. You got bored of money
a long time ago.

628
00:49:51,611 --> 00:49:53,147
Cos you know anyone can have money,

629
00:49:53,171 --> 00:49:54,251
you can fucking...

630
00:49:57,491 --> 00:50:00,187
...you can fucking find money
in the mud.

631
00:50:00,380 --> 00:50:02,060
You can forge money.

632
00:50:02,611 --> 00:50:04,891
Mr Shelby, you can steal money,
am I right?

633
00:50:06,537 --> 00:50:09,937
The currency here, it's blood.

634
00:50:12,011 --> 00:50:14,667
And Mr Shelby knows that
better than all of them.

635
00:50:14,691 --> 00:50:16,267
Blood here is like wine,

636
00:50:16,291 --> 00:50:19,467
like the vintage wine
in that bottle. It's the label,

637
00:50:19,491 --> 00:50:22,467
it's the terroir,
it's the grape that makes the wine.

638
00:50:22,491 --> 00:50:25,107
Who fucking cares
about the glass around it?

639
00:50:25,131 --> 00:50:27,667
And you, my friend, you're an American.

640
00:50:27,691 --> 00:50:29,947
You fucking smash the glass,

641
00:50:29,971 --> 00:50:31,387
you spill the blood

642
00:50:31,411 --> 00:50:33,900
and you spend their currency
to get what you want.

643
00:50:35,350 --> 00:50:36,510
Am I right?

644
00:50:38,531 --> 00:50:40,620
When you come to America,

645
00:50:41,011 --> 00:50:43,187
I will show you things.

646
00:50:43,211 --> 00:50:44,531
You're going to America?

647
00:50:47,011 --> 00:50:50,627
To Canada, Lizzie,
to collect payment for the shipment.

648
00:50:50,651 --> 00:50:52,220
I need to do it myself.

649
00:50:53,571 --> 00:50:55,467
And who will be going with you?

650
00:50:55,491 --> 00:50:58,067
Michael will be there to watch his back.

651
00:50:58,091 --> 00:51:00,660
Another journey, Tommy?

652
00:51:01,011 --> 00:51:02,667
$5 million, Mrs Shelby.

653
00:51:02,691 --> 00:51:04,731
It's worth a little cruise,
don't you think?

654
00:51:08,691 --> 00:51:12,227
You know whiskey does talk, Mr Nelson,

655
00:51:12,251 --> 00:51:15,780
and sometimes
whiskey is... very eloquent.

656
00:51:17,731 --> 00:51:21,651
But $5 million, Mr Nelson...

657
00:51:23,684 --> 00:51:25,004
Now, that is a legacy.

658
00:51:27,184 --> 00:51:30,944
And when I come back,
I will know everything.

659
00:51:33,384 --> 00:51:38,384
I see myself so clearly
in you, Thomas Shelby.

660
00:51:39,691 --> 00:51:42,827
You are a man with a bright
and glittering future.

661
00:51:46,291 --> 00:51:48,947
Mr Shelby,
there's a car coming up the drive.

662
00:51:48,971 --> 00:51:50,507
A Rolls-Royce.

663
00:51:50,531 --> 00:51:52,260
Were you expecting more guests?

664
00:51:54,051 --> 00:51:55,251
No.

665
00:52:02,537 --> 00:52:04,017
Excuse me.

666
00:52:11,891 --> 00:52:14,227
We were on our way
to my constituency in Smethwick

667
00:52:14,251 --> 00:52:16,667
and I heard our American friend
was in Birmingham

668
00:52:16,691 --> 00:52:18,467
and that he was coming here,

669
00:52:18,491 --> 00:52:22,260
so we came to say one last farewell.

670
00:52:25,284 --> 00:52:27,884
Champagne. We have much to celebrate.

671
00:52:36,091 --> 00:52:38,347
It isn't that I wasn't sure
Mr Shelby would give you

672
00:52:38,371 --> 00:52:41,187
an excellent send-off, I just felt,

673
00:52:41,211 --> 00:52:43,787
since telegrams and wires

674
00:52:43,811 --> 00:52:47,267
and letters can so easily
be intercepted,

675
00:52:47,291 --> 00:52:50,027
we might confirm all that
we've achieved during your visit

676
00:52:50,051 --> 00:52:51,531
over champagne.

677
00:52:52,651 --> 00:52:56,227
It is remarkable how quickly
our relationships have developed.

678
00:52:56,251 --> 00:52:58,907
So many triangles in this room.

679
00:52:59,257 --> 00:53:02,577
Everyone except from Mr Nelson
is the point of a triangle.

680
00:53:03,811 --> 00:53:05,867
How am I part of a triangle?

681
00:53:05,891 --> 00:53:10,027
Mr Nelson,
you have all that you came for?

682
00:53:10,051 --> 00:53:12,387
I have confirmation
that the future of Europe is in

683
00:53:12,411 --> 00:53:15,027
the hands of men like yourselves.

684
00:53:15,520 --> 00:53:19,267
And that urgent conversations
between Washington,

685
00:53:19,291 --> 00:53:22,460
Rome and of course Berlin can now begin.

686
00:53:23,691 --> 00:53:26,740
A two-week visit that may have
changed the course of history.

687
00:53:27,931 --> 00:53:29,467
We have all got what we wanted.

688
00:53:29,491 --> 00:53:31,067
Yes.

689
00:53:31,260 --> 00:53:34,771
And I got what I have wanted
from the moment I set eyes on it.

690
00:53:40,357 --> 00:53:43,677
Elizabeth, you are a very lucky woman...

691
00:53:44,524 --> 00:53:48,204
...to have each day
what I have only sampled once.

692
00:54:11,251 --> 00:54:12,667
Forgive us, Mr Nelson,

693
00:54:12,691 --> 00:54:14,740
that was a necessary bit
of housekeeping.

694
00:54:20,504 --> 00:54:21,584
Thomas.

695
00:54:23,171 --> 00:54:25,107
We do so hate to be indiscreet,

696
00:54:25,131 --> 00:54:28,387
but we have told you many times,

697
00:54:28,411 --> 00:54:33,267
if you are to seek power
in these days of shiny magazines

698
00:54:33,291 --> 00:54:35,747
and society photographs,

699
00:54:36,060 --> 00:54:38,811
sooner or later, you will have to
find a spouse who is more suitable.

700
00:54:40,491 --> 00:54:42,427
A woman with Lizzie's past

701
00:54:42,451 --> 00:54:44,891
and personal history
really isn't suitable.

702
00:54:47,657 --> 00:54:49,617
She doesn't deserve you, Mr Shelby.

703
00:55:13,691 --> 00:55:15,531
You know the thing is, Mosley...

704
00:55:17,164 --> 00:55:18,380
...you're right.

705
00:55:21,371 --> 00:55:23,140
You're right, she doesn't deserve me.

706
00:55:28,164 --> 00:55:29,644
She doesn't deserve what I am.

707
00:55:32,091 --> 00:55:34,707
She doesn't deserve what I will become.

708
00:55:35,060 --> 00:55:36,980
What will you become?

709
00:55:37,411 --> 00:55:40,307
The truth is, I belong here,
at this table.

710
00:55:40,331 --> 00:55:42,011
With fuckers like you.

711
00:55:44,797 --> 00:55:46,237
She doesn't.

712
00:55:49,390 --> 00:55:51,630
For all I try to hide it...

713
00:55:52,849 --> 00:55:54,946
...I'm just one of you.

714
00:55:59,651 --> 00:56:01,987
Could there be a sadder ending, eh?

715
00:57:02,371 --> 00:57:05,707
I'm here on behalf of your wife,
Gina, and Jack Nelson.

716
00:57:06,417 --> 00:57:08,977
Mr Nelson's prepared
to get you out of here.

717
00:57:09,411 --> 00:57:12,011
But first he needs an answer
to the question.

718
00:57:13,771 --> 00:57:15,091
If the answer is yes...

719
00:57:16,857 --> 00:57:17,977
...you'll be released.

720
00:57:20,251 --> 00:57:21,451
If the answer is no...

721
00:57:22,904 --> 00:57:24,144
...you'll stay.

722
00:57:27,251 --> 00:57:28,771
I have consulted my mother.

723
00:57:30,144 --> 00:57:31,424
Your mother's dead.

724
00:57:33,771 --> 00:57:35,531
Never the less, I have consulted her.

725
00:57:39,317 --> 00:57:40,357
And yes.

726
00:57:42,131 --> 00:57:43,187
When I'm released,

727
00:57:43,211 --> 00:57:45,340
it is my intention to kill Tommy Shelby.



## S06E06

1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:04,162
WWW.MY-SUBS.CO

﻿1
00:00:00,080 --> 00:00:01,620
Please be aware, Mr Shelby,
that the deaths of your people

2
00:00:01,660 --> 00:00:03,283
are your own responsibility.

3
00:00:03,307 --> 00:00:05,243
Since my mother
passed away four years ago,

4
00:00:05,267 --> 00:00:06,643
Tommy and I haven't even spoken.

5
00:00:06,667 --> 00:00:09,323
I'm very much looking forward to
working with you again, Michael.

6
00:00:09,347 --> 00:00:12,323
That, my friend, is the finest opium
in the world.

7

I don't need anything.

00:47:03,380 --> 00:47:05,885
Don't pick up things. Don't.

542
00:47:05,909 --> 00:47:07,229
Come here, come on.

543
00:47:13,909 --> 00:47:16,525
Emily! Emily, come on.

544
00:47:16,549 --> 00:47:19,725
If you get lost in the fog,
the Peaky Blinders will get you.

545
00:47:22,469 --> 00:47:23,829
Jeremiah...

546
00:47:25,189 --> 00:47:29,220
...let's charm the old keepsake
from Passchendaele.

547
00:47:45,669 --> 00:47:46,949
Fuck!

548
00:47:49,189 --> 00:47:50,366
Fuck!

549
00:49:01,389 --> 00:49:03,365
Come here.

550
00:49:03,389 --> 00:49:05,580
Shh...

551
00:49:08,983 --> 00:49:10,749
Breathe.

552
00:49:17,189 --> 00:49:19,429
Her name was Elizabeth Gray.

553
00:49:22,429 --> 00:49:23,885
She was my Aunt Polly.

554
00:49:25,629 --> 00:49:27,109
My Aunt Polly.

555
00:49:30,189 --> 00:49:32,029
Vengeance is for the Lord...

556
00:49:37,549 --> 00:49:40,029
Not in Small Heath, it ain't.

557
00:49:43,782 --> 00:49:45,702
Rest in peace, Pol.

558
00:50:18,269 --> 00:50:20,525
Leave us, Uncle Charlie.

559
00:50:20,716 --> 00:50:22,116
We're still in France.

560
00:51:04,929 --> 00:51:06,449
OK.

561
00:51:07,268 --> 00:51:09,460
I see him coming out of the fog.

562
00:51:30,029 --> 00:51:31,780
How was the flight?

563
00:51:32,309 --> 00:51:35,485
They say it's the future,
I'm not so sure.

564
00:51:35,509 --> 00:51:36,989
Whiskey.

565
00:51:39,229 --> 00:51:41,389
Hello, Michael.

566
00:51:42,995 --> 00:51:44,635
Tommy.

567
00:51:53,582 --> 00:51:55,782
Give me another.

568
00:51:57,869 --> 00:52:01,300
We want you to take us to where the
opium is being stored.

569
00:52:02,149 --> 00:52:05,045
And then we will provide you
with a banker's draft

570
00:52:05,069 --> 00:52:06,596
for the full amount.

571
00:52:07,729 --> 00:52:09,369
$5 million.

572
00:52:10,869 --> 00:52:12,820
$5 million.

573
00:52:13,816 --> 00:52:15,296
Let's go.

574
00:52:22,069 --> 00:52:23,845
I'll go with Tommy.

575
00:52:23,869 --> 00:52:25,549
You boys follow behind.

576
00:52:31,229 --> 00:52:34,860
Ah, shit. Forgot my cigarettes.

577
00:54:29,056 --> 00:54:30,376
Mum...

578
00:54:33,235 --> 00:54:34,980
...it's done.

579
00:54:37,336 --> 00:54:38,896
It's over.

580
00:54:41,202 --> 00:54:43,562
And may God forgive me.

581
00:55:17,349 --> 00:55:21,149
Johnny! Johnny, where are you?

582
00:55:22,962 --> 00:55:25,580
I switched the ticker
like you said, Tom.

583
00:55:29,309 --> 00:55:32,229
Tell me I've done
a good thing here, Tom.

584
00:55:43,400 --> 00:55:44,957
Goodbye, Michael.

585
00:55:44,982 --> 00:55:46,422
Goodbye, Johnny.

586
00:55:48,149 --> 00:55:49,700
You're a good man.

587
00:55:53,362 --> 00:55:57,202
I'm going to go look at the fog, Tom.

588
00:56:03,062 --> 00:56:04,782
Speak to me.

589
00:56:06,362 --> 00:56:08,242
Speak to me, Michael.

590
00:56:11,149 --> 00:56:14,685
- You killed her.
- Polly made her own choices, Michael.

591
00:56:14,709 --> 00:56:16,285
No...

592
00:56:16,309 --> 00:56:20,060
No-one close to you makes a choice
without your opinion, Tom.

593
00:56:21,989 --> 00:56:23,605
Not Arthur,

594
00:56:24,109 --> 00:56:27,109
not me, not Ada.

595
00:56:28,682 --> 00:56:30,660
We can't escape you.

596
00:56:33,508 --> 00:56:36,068
Your lethal hand is always
on our shoulders.

597
00:56:40,629 --> 00:56:42,149
Polly was half of me.

598
00:56:43,602 --> 00:56:45,562
Still visits me in my dreams.

599
00:56:47,915 --> 00:56:49,795
She'll visit me no more.

600
00:57:03,222 --> 00:57:05,662
I have no limitations.

601
00:58:10,349 --> 00:58:13,285
I smell the smell of roasting Irishmen.

602
00:58:13,940 --> 00:58:15,429
Oh, yes, hello.

603
00:58:16,629 --> 00:58:19,125
I also smell the smell of tobacco,

604
00:58:19,149 --> 00:58:21,868
which is forbidden in my presence
for all except for one,

605
00:58:21,892 --> 00:58:23,669
my new wife, Edna.

606
00:58:25,109 --> 00:58:28,245
The Irish being rendered
to smoke and fat,

607
00:58:28,269 --> 00:58:30,925
I now own half of Boston,

608
00:58:30,949 --> 00:58:36,060
so, out of respect
for my restored authority...

609
00:58:37,589 --> 00:58:40,300
...put the fucking cigarette
out now, Tommy.

610
00:58:41,869 --> 00:58:43,725
Hello, Alfie.

611
00:58:43,749 --> 00:58:45,245
I heard it was a good wedding.

612
00:58:45,269 --> 00:58:47,445
Yeah, it was, actually. Thank you.

613
00:58:47,469 --> 00:58:49,925
Edna's from a family circus.

614
00:58:49,949 --> 00:58:52,565
So, after the ketubah
and the old swapping of rings

615
00:58:52,589 --> 00:58:56,405
and the smashing of glass,
we left aboard elephants!

616
00:58:56,429 --> 00:58:58,165
Yeah, it was quite a thing.

617
00:58:58,189 --> 00:59:00,405
They had to shut down
Camden High Street,

618
00:59:00,429 --> 00:59:02,685
and even the Gentile what normally
fucking hate me,

619
00:59:02,709 --> 00:59:04,509
they waved with their hankies.

620
00:59:06,729 --> 00:59:08,049
Justice.

621
00:59:09,749 --> 00:59:13,875
And housekeeping. Long overdue.

622
00:59:14,420 --> 00:59:16,165
Yeah, look at
that little cunt ascending,

623
00:59:16,660 --> 00:59:18,645
he's ascending to the heavens!

624
00:59:18,669 --> 00:59:21,085
Right in front of us.
Before our very eyes.

625
00:59:21,109 --> 00:59:23,285
I can see with this eye. I'm not blind.

626
00:59:23,309 --> 00:59:25,565
This eye is the eye of a dead man.

627
00:59:25,589 --> 00:59:28,365
Dead men can see through life
like it was a curtain

628
00:59:28,389 --> 00:59:30,885
that billows with the flicker
of truth upon it.

629
00:59:30,909 --> 00:59:33,165
And I can see with this eye, Tommy,

630
00:59:33,189 --> 00:59:37,020
that your nephew is ascending,
and he will be forgiven.

631
00:59:37,429 --> 00:59:39,045
Unlike you,

632
00:59:39,069 --> 00:59:41,285
who, on Judgment Day,

633
00:59:41,309 --> 00:59:45,245
is probably truly fucked when the
other shoe drops.

634
00:59:45,269 --> 00:59:46,709
Hmm?

635
00:59:50,349 --> 00:59:52,469
All right, Tommy? How are you keeping?

636
00:59:54,549 --> 00:59:56,029
You know, Alfie...

637
00:59:57,820 --> 01:00:00,005
...so many people,

638
01:00:00,029 --> 01:00:01,900
so many times

639
01:00:02,189 --> 01:00:04,380
going to so much trouble to kill me.

640
01:00:05,189 --> 01:00:06,765
I'm fucking dying anyway.

641
01:00:07,140 --> 01:00:08,685
We're all dying anyway.

642
01:00:08,709 --> 01:00:10,260
No.

643
01:00:10,989 --> 01:00:14,125
Not a bullet, not a bomb,

644
01:00:14,580 --> 01:00:16,125
not a knife.

645
01:00:16,149 --> 01:00:18,405
Is it clap? Is it clap?

646
01:00:18,429 --> 01:00:21,205
No, not even that noble.

647
01:00:22,060 --> 01:00:23,285
What are you trying to say?

648
01:00:23,309 --> 01:00:26,445
I'm about to sign over
half of fucking Camden Town

649
01:00:26,469 --> 01:00:27,885
to you as part of this deal.

650
01:00:27,909 --> 01:00:31,685
Are you saying you're
just going to die in your bed?

651
01:00:31,709 --> 01:00:34,605
I'm not going to die in bed, Alfie.
Who fucking dies in bed?

652
01:00:34,629 --> 01:00:37,405
Good people die in their bed,
Tommy. Good people.

653
01:00:37,429 --> 01:00:38,909
- Good people, eh?
- Hmm.

654
01:00:40,269 --> 01:00:41,965
Good people.

655
01:00:41,989 --> 01:00:43,845
And yet here we are, Alfie,

656
01:00:44,780 --> 01:00:47,149
after all this time, just you and me.

657
01:00:50,069 --> 01:00:52,109
And I crossed the line.

658
01:00:55,355 --> 01:00:56,835
Michael.

659
01:00:58,902 --> 01:01:00,382
Polly.

660
01:01:02,542 --> 01:01:04,060
Ruby.

661
01:01:05,949 --> 01:01:11,685
Tommy, if you are about
to express profound emotion,

662
01:01:11,709 --> 01:01:14,485
you might be better served expressing it

663
01:01:14,509 --> 01:01:17,125
to someone who gives a fuck,

664
01:01:17,149 --> 01:01:20,365
or perhaps to somebody who is being paid

665
01:01:20,389 --> 01:01:22,325
to pretend to have to.

666
01:01:22,349 --> 01:01:26,660
Like a fucking nurse.
Or a priest! Someone.

667
01:01:28,829 --> 01:01:30,540
And as for death,

668
01:01:31,109 --> 01:01:33,525
speaking as someone who has been dead

669
01:01:33,549 --> 01:01:35,765
for a number of years,

670
01:01:35,789 --> 01:01:38,180
I can only heartily recommend it.

671
01:01:39,229 --> 01:01:43,780
Well, Alfie, your opera is complete.

672
01:01:50,309 --> 01:01:54,020
Shall we go and witness the final act?

673
01:02:39,476 --> 01:02:41,500
Whenever you're ready, boys.

674
01:03:24,069 --> 01:03:25,445
That's enough.

675
01:03:27,309 --> 01:03:29,029
Thank you all for coming.

676
01:03:30,709 --> 01:03:32,700
Well, at least I can say that, er...

677
01:03:34,029 --> 01:03:35,750
...I am one of those rare politicians

678
01:03:35,774 --> 01:03:38,229
who actually makes good on his promises.

679
01:03:39,949 --> 01:03:41,805
Country estate,

680
01:03:41,829 --> 01:03:46,125
requisitioned to make way
for houses for working people.

681
01:03:46,149 --> 01:03:49,493
I improved my own home
with good intentions

682
01:03:49,999 --> 01:03:52,069
and 1,500lb of dynamite.

683
01:03:57,002 --> 01:03:58,522
Now I'm back where we began...

684
01:04:00,069 --> 01:04:01,749
...with horses and caravans...

685
01:04:04,135 --> 01:04:06,020
...vagabonds and thieves.

686
01:04:10,342 --> 01:04:12,462
Frances, sit down, please.

687
01:04:21,149 --> 01:04:23,020
I'd like to raise a toast.

688
01:04:24,348 --> 01:04:25,628
A simple toast.

689
01:04:28,909 --> 01:04:30,325
To family.

690
01:04:30,500 --> 01:04:32,045
- To family.
- To family.

691
01:04:32,069 --> 01:04:36,420
Sometimes it is shelter from the storm.

692
01:04:38,248 --> 01:04:40,500
Sometimes it is the storm itself.

693
01:04:51,342 --> 01:04:53,140
I'm planning on going away for a bit.

694
01:04:54,835 --> 01:04:56,555
After I'm gone...

695
01:05:00,020 --> 01:05:01,380
Ada...

696
01:05:02,402 --> 01:05:03,762
...in this family...

697
01:05:04,922 --> 01:05:07,322
...it was you who was born
to be a politician, not me.

698
01:05:09,249 --> 01:05:10,729
Remember that.

699
01:05:12,140 --> 01:05:14,285
And if ever a seat
is to become available

700
01:05:14,309 --> 01:05:16,725
in this ugly old city, you should run.

701
01:05:18,656 --> 01:05:19,712
Where's Arthur?

702
01:05:19,737 --> 01:05:21,940
He went for a walk down the river.

703
01:05:22,669 --> 01:05:24,506
He said he's not good at farewells

704
01:05:24,531 --> 01:05:27,470
so he's decided to
go catch a trout instead.

705
01:05:31,082 --> 01:05:33,202
He told me to tell you that...

706
01:05:35,295 --> 01:05:38,335
"Where you're going, Tommy,
there will I be...

707
01:05:39,442 --> 01:05:42,082
"..very soon. Love, Arthur."

708
01:05:49,016 --> 01:05:51,580
How does Arthur know
where you're going, Tommy?

709
01:05:53,620 --> 01:05:55,380
You watch him, Linda.

710
01:05:56,295 --> 01:05:57,660
You love him.

711
01:06:02,029 --> 01:06:06,165
Charles, I want you
to look after your mum.

712
01:06:06,860 --> 01:06:09,389
You tell her I'm sorry, you hear me?

713
01:06:15,642 --> 01:06:17,722
I want you to be the bes...

714
01:06:21,829 --> 01:06:25,229
Exactly how long
are you going away for, Tommy?

715
01:06:35,589 --> 01:06:37,189
Thanks, Curly.

716
01:06:54,509 --> 01:06:56,205
Tom, the horse.

717
01:06:56,229 --> 01:06:57,869
Shut up, Curly.

718
01:07:04,949 --> 01:07:06,900
Is she hitched, Johnny?

719
01:07:08,260 --> 01:07:11,180
Tommy, you tell me right now,
where are you going?

720
01:07:11,669 --> 01:07:14,565
You have to carry the bucket
on your own this time, Ada.

721
01:07:14,589 --> 01:07:16,445
Tommy, you come to me with everything.

722
01:07:16,469 --> 01:07:19,845
- You always come to me.
- Not this time. Not this one, sister.

723
01:07:20,202 --> 01:07:23,322
What the fuck does that mean?
Where are you going?

724
01:07:24,822 --> 01:07:26,822
Tommy!

725
01:07:34,149 --> 01:07:36,709
_

726
01:11:37,669 --> 01:11:42,109
In the bleak midwinter...

727
01:11:44,989 --> 01:11:47,469
Dad... Dad, come out, come out!

728
01:11:48,709 --> 01:11:50,309
Dad, it's me.

729
01:12:04,469 --> 01:12:06,109
Did Polly send you?

730
01:12:07,829 --> 01:12:09,580
Did Polly send you?

731
01:12:10,309 --> 01:12:11,685
Or am I dead already?

732
01:12:12,149 --> 01:12:13,429
No.

733
01:12:15,155 --> 01:12:16,860
You're not dead.

734
01:12:17,669 --> 01:12:19,845
You're not even sick.

735
01:12:20,102 --> 01:12:21,582
But I am, my darling.

736
01:12:23,375 --> 01:12:24,815
I'm sick.

737
01:12:25,909 --> 01:12:27,325
Sick like you was.

738
01:12:27,349 --> 01:12:29,525
No. Not true.

739
01:12:29,549 --> 01:12:32,349
I know it. You've got to live, Daddy.

740
01:12:35,069 --> 01:12:37,149
You let the fire go out.

741
01:12:39,500 --> 01:12:41,845
Light the fire again and get warm,

742
01:12:41,869 --> 01:12:45,029
and you will see that you must live.

743
01:13:47,309 --> 01:13:50,005
You're not even sick, Daddy.

744
01:14:26,688 --> 01:14:28,768
Fucking Gypsies.

745
01:14:36,900 --> 01:14:39,005
Have you thrown the tinkers off
the top field yet?

746
01:14:39,029 --> 01:14:41,885
Well, I went up to the caravan,
sir, but there was no-one there.

747
01:14:41,909 --> 01:14:44,405
Well, go back up there
and set fire to the fucking thing.

748
01:14:44,429 --> 01:14:45,980
Yes, sir.

749
01:14:52,336 --> 01:14:54,620
Have you filled the car with petrol?

750
01:15:02,029 --> 01:15:05,229
I said, have you filled the car up
with petrol?

751
01:15:08,669 --> 01:15:10,709
How was the wedding in Berlin?

752
01:15:13,229 --> 01:15:15,869
I hear Chancellor Hitler
himself was the best man.

753
01:15:18,389 --> 01:15:21,780
You've been my doctor now
for three years.

754
01:15:23,229 --> 01:15:25,725
Never knew you were so well connected.

755
01:15:25,749 --> 01:15:28,165
Oh, and the doctor at St Thomas's

756
01:15:28,189 --> 01:15:30,245
who you sent me to
for the second opinion,

757
01:15:30,269 --> 01:15:32,285
second set of X-rays?

758
01:15:32,700 --> 01:15:35,260
A maid of honour at the same wedding.

759
01:15:35,949 --> 01:15:38,060
All so very well fucking connected.

760
01:15:40,262 --> 01:15:41,982
On your knees, Holford.

761
01:15:47,909 --> 01:15:50,365
I'm guessing you people all decided

762
01:15:50,389 --> 01:15:52,725
that the only person

763
01:15:52,749 --> 01:15:55,260
who could ever kill Tommy Shelby

764
01:15:56,069 --> 01:15:57,989
is Tommy Shelby himself.

765
01:16:01,069 --> 01:16:03,485
You made me believe death was coming.

766
01:16:04,102 --> 01:16:06,622
Let my nature do the rest, eh?

767
01:16:11,029 --> 01:16:13,860
You may not have tuberculoma, Mr Shelby,

768
01:16:15,142 --> 01:16:16,782
but you are sick.

769
01:16:17,702 --> 01:16:19,182
I know you.

770
01:16:20,275 --> 01:16:21,980
You are sick with guilt.

771
01:16:24,115 --> 01:16:27,115
Sick of death at your own hand.

772
01:16:28,682 --> 01:16:30,442
Sick of who you were.

773
01:16:33,069 --> 01:16:34,845
You are no longer the kind of man

774
01:16:34,869 --> 01:16:37,460
who would kill another man
in cold blood.

775
01:16:43,029 --> 01:16:47,020
Tommy, you have been on a journey

776
01:16:47,435 --> 01:16:50,955
from the backstreets
to the corridors of power.

777
01:16:53,322 --> 01:16:54,922
You cannot go back.

778
01:16:56,589 --> 01:16:58,469
You are a different man.

779
01:16:59,929 --> 01:17:02,449
The gun no longer belongs in your hand.

780
01:17:09,062 --> 01:17:10,862
Oh, but I am back.

781
01:17:13,429 --> 01:17:15,500
Back from under the ground.

782
01:17:17,602 --> 01:17:19,140
Close your eyes.

783
01:17:22,369 --> 01:17:24,169
Close your eyes.

784
01:17:47,342 --> 01:17:49,062
The eleventh hour.

785
01:17:50,589 --> 01:17:52,140
Armistice.

786
01:17:55,036 --> 01:17:56,876
Peace at last.

787
01:17:59,889 --> 01:18:01,809
Peace at last.
